title: Weekly POC debrief - rate limit oscillation and timeout tuning
summary: Weekly POC sync to review last week's incident where we saw intermittent 5xxs and client-side timeouts during a midday burst. Team validated adaptive retry changes, discussed rate-limit oscillation driven by bursty clients and a misconfigured client-side retry policy, and agreed on benchmark runs and a short pilot config change for prefix caching and reduced max concurrency.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-19 14:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (SE), Marcus (SE), Marta (Arcadia ML), Ethan (Arcadia Platform), Leila (Arcadia CTO)
Shared links: benchmark spreadsheet: https://redwood.example/benchmarks/arcadia-poc-aug2026 (shared), security deck: redwood-security-v3.pdf

Summary (auto): incident debrief for 2026-08-12 12:15 outage, walk through telemetry, reproduce, and next steps.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, I know this is a busy window, gonna try to keep to 45, uh 50 minutes; quick roll call?
[00:12] Marta: Marta here, hi.
[00:14] Ethan: Ethan, platform.
[00:15] Leila: Leila — hi all.
[00:17] Priya: Priya from Redwood, Marcus is also on for the deep debugging.
[00:24] Jordan: cool. quick context for folks maybe who missed last week: arcadia saw a midday spike where many requests got 5xx and client timeouts spiked to like 6% for a ~20 minute window. we traced a pattern to— there was backpressure in the serving lanes and then a reactive retry fan-out from your side, which made it worse. today we want to validate mitigations and agree next steps.
[00:45] Marta: yeah thanks, we pulled traces. looks like a subset of endpoints with long seq_len and large embedding calls that are slower. the client's retry policy was short interval, no jitter, so they retried quickly and amplified requests.
[01:03] Ethan: to add, our ingress autoscaler was hanging on a pod that was stuck due to GPU oom-ish behaviour, not sure if it was oom but it wasn't releasing memory, so concurrency dropped to 40% for a short bit.
[01:18] Marcus: small correction, we saw kernel timeouts on the model shard that processed long context, so that matched. also some KV cache misses because of prefix variance.
[01:32] Priya: ok so two levers -- client-side backoff and server-side shaping + caching. we pushed an adaptive backoff to your test cluster last night, can you confirm results?
[01:45] Marta: we ran a synthetic burst and i saw fewer 5xxs but the latency tail still moved from 220ms to 480ms for some requests. variability is still high.
[01:58] Jordan: thanks, that's helpful. Marcus, do you have the telemetry summary?
[02:03] Marcus: yes, baseline P50 ~60ms, P95 ~310ms during steady state. during the burst we hit P95 ~650ms, P99 >1.2s for long seq. 5xxs aligned with connection resets in the worker logs and we saw a climb in queue length before the errors. also, there was an interaction with your client retries — saw a near-doubling of inflight requests when retry fan-out kicked in.
[02:32] Ethan: couple clarifying Qs — how aggressive was the retry we pushed last night?
[02:36] Priya: we set exponential backoff starting 200ms with jitter, cap at 2s, max retries 3. Before you had immediate retry at 100ms and no cap.
[02:46] Ethan: right that old behavior is definitely the amplifier.
[02:48] Marta: one odd thing — some 5xx were 502 from the front proxy, others are 504s at the worker. logs are noisy so mapping is tricky.
[02:58] Jordan: yep, typical. question for Arcadia — is data residency or private deployment still in scope? i recall Leila preferred a VPC for HIPAA compliance, is that still the plan or is hosted ok?
[03:12] Leila: still prefer VPC, we can do hosted but need isolated networking and key management, SOC2 and audit logs. we'll bring that into procurement soon.
[03:24] Jordan: ok good. that matters because it changes routing and fallback options.
[03:28] Priya: back to incident, one mitigation we proposed is to reduce max concurrency at gateway level for long-seq endpoints and enable prefix KV cache for common prompts to drop token computation. that reduces per-request work and smooths the tail.
[03:47] Marta: how intrusive is KV cache? are you meaning you cache kv states for recent prefixes? will that change correctness for dynamic prompts?
[03:56] Marcus: it's prefix-aware cache, you can opt in per route. for dynamic prompts we don't cache unless you configure stable prefixes — we gave a config last week in the shared sheet. there's a small risk if prompts are user-specific, but for system prompts and templates it's safe.
[04:13] Ethan: timeline Q — if we flip cache on for two endpoints today for canary, how quickly can we roll back?
[04:19] Priya: immediate rollback, it's config-level. you can test in staging and then flip. no model restarts.
[04:24] Marta: ok let's do that for /note-gen and /summarize, those are heavy.
[04:30] Leila: what's the expected unit cost impact? if we use caching and reduce compute that's good but i'm also worried about added infra for caching.
[04:40] Jordan: cache reduces token compute, so per-token GPU cost goes down; small memory overhead in workers. overall we expect net cost reduction for those endpoints because they are compute heavy. we can quantify in the benchmark.
[04:54] Marcus: we attached a cost model in the shared sheet — look at the 'kv-cache-scenarios' tab.
[05:02] Marta: another question — we saw client idempotency causing duplicates because retries changed payload IDs. any best practices?
[05:09] Priya: recommend using idempotency keys or request IDs. also staggered retry jitter as we mentioned.
[05:16] Ethan: ok we will add idempotency.
[05:18] Jordan: on the server side, one recurring pattern is rate-limit oscillation: when a subset of clients back off, tokens drop and the rate limiter loosens, then more aggressive clients surge again and it repeats — causing those short windows of instability. we can implement a short-term smoothing window on the rate limiter to avoid immediate oscillation.
[05:40] Marcus: yes smoothing window of ~10s helps. we can also bias rate limits by route priority.
[05:47] Marta: does smoothing increase observed latency?
[05:49] Marcus: slight increase in steady P95, but far fewer 5xx spikes and better tail stability. tradeoff is predictable latency vs spikes.
[05:58] Leila: for our SLA we care about 99th percentile — we prefer stable P99 over occasional lower P95 but high P99.
[06:06] Jordan: got it. that informs our config suggestions.
[06:10] Ethan: any notes on kernel-level upgrades? we saw a couple of worker restarts correlated with driver warnings last week.
[06:16] Priya: we shipped a micro-patch to guard against a rare kernel scheduling block — it's optional in the config and we recommended it for long-context models. Marcus can share the patch ID.
[06:26] Marcus: patch id: rwinf-kw-2026-08-15, changelog in the shared doc.
[06:31] Marta: curious about the retry budget concept you mentioned earlier — can you recap?
[06:34] Jordan: sure — a retry budget limits the number of retries per client over a sliding window, so a single misbehaving client can't amplify errors. combine with adaptive backoff and jitter and you reduce fan-out.
[06:46] Ethan: makes sense.
[06:47] Priya: on the test you ran last night, Marta, can you confirm the config we applied?
[06:52] Marta: yes: adaptive backoff as you described, smoothing window at 10s, reduced max concurrency on the long-seq route from 64 to 24, kv-cache enabled for certain prefixes.
[07:04] Jordan: then the ask for this week is to run deterministic benchmarks and a replay of the burst workload. can you run two sets — one with old client retry (for baseline) one with new adaptive backoff? we'll compare.
[07:16] Marta: yes. we have a replay harness but need the exact traffic pattern from last week — can you share the traces?
[07:22] Marcus: shared link: https://redwood.example/traces/arcadia-20260812-burst (note: access via your account).
[07:30] Marta: got it. we'll run both and post results.
[07:33] Leila: also can we get the security checklist for VPC deployment? procurement will want SOC2 evidence and key management details.
[07:40] Jordan: yes we'll send the security deck and SOC2 artifacts. shared earlier but will reattach.
[07:46] Ethan: question re: failover — if we put primary model on dedicated nodes, can we failover to a cheaper quantized variant to keep latency low when load spikes?
[07:55] Priya: yes, Redwood supports model variants and automatic fallback. we can set cost-based routing to degrade to a quantized variant with slightly lower quality but much higher throughput. that is a config change and can be tuned per-route.
[08:08] Marta: ok that is promising. we want to test quality delta.
[08:12] Jordan: we'll include A/B quality tests in the benchmark plan.
[08:15] Marcus: quick note — we saw an instance where a client's aggressive concurrency pattern bypassed the rate limiter because requests hit different worker shards; we're iterating on a cluster-wide token bucket to avoid that sharding hole.
[08:30] Ethan: good catch. that explains our spike.
[08:33] Priya: wrapping to actions: we'll agree on a short run book: 1) enable kv cache on canary endpoints, 2) flip smoothing window, 3) run replayed burst with two client configs, 4) run quantized fallback test, 5) send security docs.
[08:48] Leila: timeline — we need a summary to procurement by next Wed.
[08:52] Jordan: next Wed is 2026-08-26, we'll aim for that.
[08:56] Marta: one more small bug — we noticed some mis-attributed speaker labels in logs, not critical but annoying for debugging.
[09:03] Marcus: noted.
[09:05] Jordan: ok let's do quick round robin on owners for the actions.
[09:09] Ethan: i'll own the client replay runs and idempotency key rollout, due 2026-08-24.
[09:15] Marta: i'll run the benchmarks and post to the sheet, due 2026-08-25.
[09:19] Leila: procurement summary run by me, due 2026-08-26.
[09:23] Priya: i'll prepare the fallback config for quantized variant and share test instructions, due 2026-08-24.
[09:29] Jordan: i'll send the security artifacts and the consolidated action list, due 2026-08-20 EOD.
[09:36] Marcus: i'll follow up on the kernel patch and cluster-wide token bucket ETA, target 2026-08-27.
[09:43] Jordan: any other Qs?
[09:44] Leila: none here.
[09:46] Marta: no.
[09:47] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll reconvene same time next week unless we need an interim hotfix call.

Recap / Next steps on call:
- Enable kv cache on /note-gen and /summarize canary routes (low-risk config)
- Apply smoothing window to rate limiter (10s) and reduced max concurrency for long-seq routes
- Replay the burst with old vs new client retry for comparison
- Run quantized fallback A/B quality tests
- Share SOC2 and VPC deployment checklist to procurement

End transcript.
